articles.title: Tragedy in Gurugram: 8-Year-Old Crushed by School Van While Returning Home
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a heartbreaking incident in the Bhondsi area of Gurugram, an eight-year-old boy lost his life after being run over by a school van on Wednesday morning.

body.html:
In a heartbreaking incident in the Bhondsi area of Gurugram, an eight-year-old boy lost his life after being run over by a school van on Wednesday morning.

The deceased child, Shivansh Tripathi, was a Class 1 student of Laburnum Public School and lived with his family in Shyam Kunj, Maruti Kunj.

According to the complaint filed by his father, Santosh Kumar Tripathi, the family hails from Ambedkar Nagar district in Uttar Pradesh and is currently residing in Gurugram.

As per the complaint, Shivansh had returned home from school around 8 am and later went to his father’s nearby grocery shop to buy chocolates. While returning home, a Maruti Eeco van belonging to a private school allegedly reversed at high speed in a reckless manner and struck the child.

The impact knocked him to the ground, and the driver reportedly ran over him, causing severe head and body injuries. Locals rushed to the spot after hearing the child’s cries and pulled him out from under the vehicle.

He was immediately taken to Medanta Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

Police have registered a case against the driver based on the father’s complaint and initiated an investigation into the incident.

The tragedy has sparked outrage among residents, raising serious concerns over negligent driving, especially involving school vehicles in residential areas.

articles.title: ₹5 Lakh Gone in Minutes! Farmer Robbed While Buying Onions in Palnadu district
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking incident, an unidentified person stole ₹5 lakh in cash from a farmer’s scooty near Jonnalagadda bypass in Narasaraopet, triggering concern over public safety.

body.html:
In a shocking incident, an unidentified person stole ₹5 lakh in cash from a farmer’s scooty near Jonnalagadda bypass in Narasaraopet, triggering concern over public safety.

The victim, Venkata Satyanarayana, a resident of Vemuluripadu village in Firangipuram mandal, had reportedly borrowed the amount from relatives for financial needs.

According to reports, while returning to his hometown with the cash, he stopped at Jonnalagadda bypass to purchase onions. He parked his scooty outside a shop and went inside briefly. During this time, an unidentified आरोपी opened the vehicle’s dickey, stole the ₹5 lakh kept inside, and fled the spot.

The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed in the area.

Following the theft, the victim lodged a complaint at the local police station in Narasaraopet. Police have initiated an investigation and are examining CCTV footage to identify the accused.

The incident has raised concerns about safety and vigilance, especially while carrying large amounts of cash in public places.

(According to CCTV 04 April 2026)

articles.title: Accident or Conspiracy? Asgar Ali Death Sparks Uproar in Agra
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The case of the suspicious death of transport businessman Asgar Ali in Agra is intensifying, with the family alleging murder while police continue to treat it as a road accident. Asgar Ali died late Friday night after being hit by a car.

body.html:
The case of the suspicious death of transport businessman Asgar Ali in Agra is intensifying, with the family alleging murder while police continue to treat it as a road accident.

Asgar Ali died late Friday night after being hit by a car. However, his family has rejected the accident theory, claiming it was a pre-planned conspiracy. They have accused GST Assistant Commissioner Nivedita Singh and her husband, Dr. Ajay Pal Yadav, of involvement in the alleged murder.

A new CCTV footage has surfaced, adding to the controversy. The video reportedly shows Asgar Ali walking towards his warehouse around 3 am, when a speeding car approaches from behind and hits him.

The family claims that the act was deliberate, pointing out that several other vehicles passed through the same stretch without incident. They also allege that there was no horn or visible attempt by the driver to avoid the collision, raising further suspicion.

According to the family, tensions had escalated a day before the incident when Asgar Ali held a press conference against GST officials. They allege that his vehicle was seized again the following day without proper verification, suggesting possible harassment.

A complaint has been filed by Abdul Ali against two alleged journalists, the GST officer, and her husband, demanding a fair probe. However, no FIR has been registered so far, leading to anger among family members.

Meanwhile, Ali Abbas stated that the CCTV footage prima facie indicates a road accident. He added that if a second complaint is filed, appropriate legal action and investigation will be initiated.

The case continues to raise serious questions, with the family demanding a thorough and impartial investigation.

#Agra #BreakingNews #CrimeNews #CCTVFootage #JusticeDemanded

articles.title: Storm Turns Deadly: Pilgrims’ Car Crashes Into Lorry Near Palasa, Two Critical
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A horrific road accident on Sunday evening along the national highway near Palasa in Srikakulam left three persons injured, two of them in critical condition, after a car lost control and collided with a lorry amid severe weather conditions.

body.html:
A horrific road accident on Sunday evening along the national highway near Palasa in Srikakulam left three persons injured, two of them in critical condition, after a car lost control and collided with a lorry amid severe weather conditions.

The incident occurred near the Nemali Narayanapuram bypass when a Toyota Innova, carrying pilgrims returning from the Jagannath Temple, veered off course during heavy rain and strong winds.

The injured have been identified as Mukesh Panigrahi, Amulya Patro, and driver Achyutananda Barada, all residents of Parlakhemundi.

According to reports, torrential rainfall and gusty winds reduced visibility and made roads slippery. The driver reportedly lost control due to the storm, causing the vehicle to mount the divider and enter the opposite lane, where it collided head-on with a speeding lorry.

The impact was severe, leaving the car mangled. The vehicle overturned multiple times before crashing into nearby agricultural fields.

Locals and passersby rushed to the spot and rescued the trapped occupants before informing emergency services. The injured were initially taken to Palasa Government Hospital.

Due to the seriousness of their injuries, Mukesh Panigrahi and Achyutananda Barada, who suffered severe head and internal injuries, were later shifted to Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences for advanced treatment. Their condition remains critical.

Police from Kasibugga Police Station have registered a case and initiated an investigation. Circle Inspector Y. Ramakrishna stated that preliminary findings indicate overspeeding combined with sudden storm conditions may have caused the vehicle to hydroplane, leading to the loss of control.

The lorry driver is currently being questioned as part of the ongoing probe.

#AndhraPradesh #RoadAccident #BreakingNews #Srikakulam

body.html:
A woman staged a protest outside her boyfriend’s residence in Mahabubabad district after he allegedly refused to marry her despite being in a long-term relationship.

The incident took place in Gudur mandal and created a stir in the local area.

The woman, identified as Guguloth Spandana from Rekula Thanda in Kesamudram mandal, had reportedly been in a relationship for the past seven years with Tejavat Raghuram, a resident of Vagya Thanda in Gudur mandal.

According to sources, their friendship gradually developed into a romantic relationship, and the couple spent several years together. It is alleged that Raghuram had promised to marry Spandana.

However, when the matter of marriage was raised, he reportedly refused and started distancing himself, following which the woman staged a protest outside his house.

There is no clarity yet on whether an official complaint has been filed. Further details are awaited.

A mobile shop owner, identified as Nikhilbhai, fell into a roadside gutter after its cover suddenly collapsed near Pardi Char Rasta on National Highway 48 in South Gujarat.

The incident occurred when Nikhilbhai was passing through the area and stepped onto a gutter cover that gave way without warning, causing him to fall into the drain.

Locals have expressed anger over the negligence and are demanding immediate action from authorities to repair the damaged infrastructure and prevent further mishaps.

articles.title: CCTV Horror in Solapur: Two Killed as Truck Crushes Bike in Seconds
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tragic road accident in Solapur claimed the lives of two persons after a truck collided with a motorcycle near Boramani Naka, sending shockwaves among local residents. The deceased have been identified as Saipan Patel and Huzur Patel.

body.html:
A tragic road accident in Solapur claimed the lives of two persons after a truck collided with a motorcycle near Boramani Naka, sending shockwaves among local residents.

The deceased have been identified as Saipan Patel and Huzur Patel. According to eyewitnesses, the collision was extremely severe, leaving both riders with critical injuries and resulting in their death on the spot.

CCTV footage from the area has captured the entire incident. Those who have seen the video described it as disturbing, showing how the crash occurred within seconds, leaving the riders with no time to react.

Police reached the spot shortly after receiving information and have initiated an investigation into the incident.

The video has since gone viral on social media, with many expressing grief over the loss of lives. Several users highlighted the dangers faced by two-wheeler riders near heavy vehicles, especially due to blind spots, while others pointed to reckless driving and poor traffic discipline.

Some also stressed that truck drivers must exercise caution, particularly while turning, to avoid such fatal accidents.

The incident has once again raised serious concerns over road safety, with calls for stricter adherence to traffic rules, better road conditions, and increased awareness among all road users to prevent such tragedies.

articles.title: ‘Custody Turned Killing Ground’: 9 Policemen Get Death Penalty in Sathankulam Custodial Death Case
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a landmark judgment, the First Additional District and Sessions Court in Madurai has sentenced nine police personnel to death in the high-profile Sathankulam Custodial Death Case, terming it a grave violation of human rights. The case pertains to the deaths of P.

body.html:
In a landmark judgment, the First Additional District and Sessions Court in Madurai has sentenced nine police personnel to death in the high-profile Sathankulam Custodial Death Case, terming it a grave violation of human rights.

The case pertains to the deaths of P. Jayaraj (58) and his son J. Bennix (31), who died in police custody in June 2020 in Sathankulam.

Pronouncing the sentence, Judge G. Muthukumaran observed that the accused, entrusted with maintaining law and order, had themselves violated the law and subjected the victims to brutal assault. The court held that the case fell under the “rarest of rare” category, warranting capital punishment. It also ordered a compensation of ₹1.40 crore to be paid to the victims’ family.

The court had earlier, on March 23, convicted the accused under multiple sections of the IPC, including murder and destruction of evidence. The judgment relied heavily on medical and forensic evidence, which established that the deaths were caused by custodial torture and not due to natural causes, as claimed by the defence.

According to the prosecution, the incident began on June 18, 2020, when police allegedly confronted individuals near Jayaraj’s shop during COVID-19 lockdown enforcement. Following an altercation, Jayaraj was taken into custody, and his son Bennix was detained the next day. Both were allegedly subjected to severe custodial assault inside the police station.

The case triggered nationwide outrage, leading to intervention by the Madras High Court, which transferred the investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation. The CBI later filed a detailed chargesheet after an extensive probe.

The trial spanned nearly five years, with over 50 witnesses examined and substantial documentary and forensic evidence presented. The court rejected the defence’s claims of accidental or natural death, noting that the injuries were consistent with repeated assault.

The verdict is being seen as a strong message against custodial violence and police excesses, reaffirming that no individual is above the law.

#SathankulamCase #CustodialDeath #BreakingNews #HumanRights

articles.title: Highway Horror! Youths Perform Deadly Car Stunts on NH-9, Viral Video Sparks Police Crackdown
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A case of dangerous stunts involving moving vehicles was reported on the Delhi–Moradabad National Highway (NH-9) in Garhmukteshwar on Sunday night, where several youth's were seen risking lives by jumping out of car windows and climbing onto rooftops.

body.html:
A case of dangerous stunts involving moving vehicles was reported on the Delhi–Moradabad National Highway (NH-9) in Garhmukteshwar on Sunday night, where several youth's were seen risking lives by jumping out of car windows and climbing onto rooftops.

According to reports, the incident took place around 8 pm near the Brajghat toll plaza, involving multiple cars travelling from Delhi towards Moradabad. Eyewitnesses said the youth's were changing lanes at high speed, shouting from windows and sitting on rooftops, posing a serious threat to other commuters and pedestrians.

A video of the incident soon went viral on social media, prompting swift action from the police.

Taking cognisance, the police launched an investigation. Kotwali police station in-charge Inspector Devendra Bisht said that efforts are underway to identify the vehicles by tracing registration numbers through CCTV footage installed along the highway, along with the viral video.

He warned that those violating traffic norms and endangering public safety will not be spared. Strict legal action will be taken against the accused once identified.
